current.title: Corpus spongiosum · bulb/shaft source · X-ray: lumen and surrounding tissue · draft
current.body: A urethrogram uses radiographic contrast to show the urethral passage in projection. The corpus spongiosum is erectile tissue around that passage, not the contrast outline. This atlas selection is a source-labelled bulb/shaft surface, not an acquired radiograph.
bullets: In typical anatomy the spongy urethra passes through the single ventral corpus spongiosum; the paired corpora cavernosa are separate columns.
The mesh does not include the separately supplied glans or cavernous surfaces. Its nearby urethra selection is context, not a verified enclosed lumen.
No contrast study, patient image, coordinate registration, lumen continuity, calibre, patency or injury finding is represented here.

Visible source limit: Original source-labelled bulb/shaft representation. The separately supplied glans and corporal surfaces are not added; this is not the complete corpus spongiosum or penis. The existing urethra is context, not a validated enclosed lumen. Original coordinates and faces retained; clinical review pending.

Reference and reuse: Original educational synthesis from NCI SEER Training Modules: Penis and Coccolini et al., Kidney and uro-trauma: WSES-AAST guidelines (2019, CC BY 4.0). WSES-AAST material was adapted in wording and limited to imaging context; no figure, table, algorithm or clinical instruction was used. No endorsement is implied.
current.note: Source-bound educational draft for revision-bound radiologist review. Bulb/shaft representation only; no glans or paired cavernous surfaces. No acquired scan, patient image, lumen continuity, calibre, patency, injury finding or coordinate registration is represented. Atlas, imaging-case and paid-lecture access remain independent.
